candidates.spoken: Why one failure blacked out 7 million people.
The blackout left nearly seven million people without power.
Grid managers maintain stability through the n-1 criterion.
But operators thought they'd have 30 minutes to react.
San Diego County alone had 1.4 million customers dark.
Grids plan to survive any single failure, the n-1 rule.
Overloads cascaded faster than anyone could react.
It was the largest power failure in California history.
Operators plan for the n-1 rule.
The cascade moved far faster than that.
What stops if grid control room stops?
In 2011, it hit San Diego, Arizona and Mexico.
That's why grid safety depends on what operators can see.
